findings.message: The batch has a payment of 2500 USD, but its totals give none for USD, so a bank that checks the totals of the batch refuses it. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Work out the totals again from the rows, and find the row that was added or lost before the batch is sent.
findings.own: comparing the totals of a batch with its rows is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a control total is how many banks and providers catch a changed file, and no cited page sets the rule

findings.message: The batch gives a total of 6082 EUR, but its 10 payments in EUR add up to 5982. A batch whose control total is off is refused by the bank, or a row was added or lost on the way. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Work out the totals again from the rows, and find the row that was added or lost before the batch is sent.
findings.own: comparing the totals of a batch with its rows is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a control total is how many banks and providers catch a changed file, and no cited page sets the rule

findings.message: The iban of payment P-002, GR1601101250000000012300696, fails the check of ISO 13616: the remainder of MOD 97-10 is 28, not 1, so a character is wrong or two are swapped. A bank may return or reject the payment.
findings.fix: Copy the IBAN again from the beneficiary, in electronic form or in groups of four; never correct the check digits by hand to make it pass.

basis.text: To check the two check digits, the communique moves the first four characters to the end, turns every letter into a number from 10 for A to 35 for Z, and asks that the result divided by 97 leave 1, the MOD 97-10 of ISO 7064.
basis.source: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkiye: Communique on the International Bank Account Number

basis.text: The communique lets a bank return or reject a transfer order whose IBAN fails that check.
basis.source: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkiye: Communique on the International Bank Account Number

findings.message: The iban of payment P-003 has 17 characters, but the IBAN registry of Swift gives NL IBANs 18.
findings.fix: Copy the IBAN again from the beneficiary; an IBAN of the right country always has the length of the registry.

basis.text: ISO named Swift the registration authority for the national formats of the IBAN, and the registry Swift publishes holds the format of each country whose IBAN follows ISO 13616.

For every country it covers, the registry gives the two letters an IBAN starts with, its structure, its length in electronic form and an example; an IBAN of Norway has 15 characters and one of Saint Lucia 32.

findings.message: The bic of payment P-005, "EXMP GB2L", has 9 characters, not 8 or 11. A BIC of ISO 9362 is four letters or digits, two letters of a country, two letters or digits, and an optional branch code of three.
findings.fix: Copy the BIC again from the bank of the beneficiary, in capitals and with no spaces.

basis.text: ISO 9362 defines the BIC as eight characters, four letters or digits for the party, two letters for a country code of ISO 3166-1 and two letters or digits after them, with a branch code of three more characters that may be added.

findings.message: The currency of payment P-007 is "EUX", which is not an alphabetic code of the ISO 4217 list SIX keeps. A bank refuses a payment in a currency it does not know.
findings.fix: Write the three capital letters of the currency as list one of ISO 4217 gives them, such as EUR, USD or JPY.

basis.text: List one of ISO 4217, kept by SIX as the maintenance agency, names for each country or entity its currency with an alphabetic code of three letters, a numeric code and a minor unit.
basis.source: SIX: ISO 4217 list one, current currency and funds code list

findings.message: The amount of payment P-008 is 150000.50 JPY, with 1 decimal place, but the ISO 4217 list gives JPY a minor unit of 0: it has no fractions. A bank refuses the amount or rounds it.
findings.fix: Round the amount to the minor unit of the currency before the batch is sent, and make sure the rounding is the one the beneficiary is owed.

basis.text: The minor unit of the list is the number of decimal places a currency is counted in: 0 for the Japanese yen, 2 for the euro, 3 for the Kuwaiti dinar, and N.A. for codes such as gold that have no fraction.
basis.source: SIX: ISO 4217 list one, current currency and funds code list

findings.message: The amount of payment P-009 is negative (-200.00); a payout pays out, and a reversal or a fee belongs in a file of its own. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Write the amount as a plain decimal number above 0, such as 1500.00, and move reversals and fees to a file of their own.
findings.own: refusing an amount of 0, a negative amount and an amount in another notation is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; none of the cited pages sets a rule on how a batch writes an amount

findings.message: The beneficiaryCountry of payment P-010 is "UK", which is not a two-letter code of the country table the tool reads (the ISO alpha-2 codes of the UN M49 table). The code of the United Kingdom is GB.
findings.fix: Write the two capital letters of the country, such as GB for the United Kingdom.

basis.text: The M49 table of the UN Statistics Division gives each country or area it lists a number of three digits and its ISO codes of two and of three letters.
basis.source: United Nations Statistics Division: Standard country or area codes for statistical use (M49)

findings.message: The paymentId P-001 is also the id of the payment at line 19; a bank or a payout provider refuses the second, or pays both when it takes the id for a new instruction. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Give every payment an id of its own and keep it the same when the batch is sent again, so that a provider can refuse a payment it has already made.
findings.own: asking for an id of its own for each payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; providers use the id to find a payment and to refuse one sent twice, and no cited page sets the rule

findings.message: Payment P-013 has no beneficiaryName, so the payment cannot be screened against sanctions lists and the bank of the beneficiary cannot match it to the account holder. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Give the full name of the beneficiary as the bank or the wallet provider knows it.
findings.own: asking for a name on every payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the name is what sanctions screening and the bank of the beneficiary read, and the cited pages are about codes and accounts

findings.message: The walletAddress of payment P-016 on Ethereum, "0x1234", has 4 characters after 0x, not 40; an address on Ethereum is 0x followed by 40 hex digits, not the zero address. A payment to it fails, or goes to an address no one holds.
findings.fix: Copy the wallet address again from the beneficiary, and confirm it with a small test payment before a large one.

basis.text: An Ethereum address is made from the last 20 bytes of a Keccak-256 hash of the public key with 0x in front, 42 characters with 40 hex digits, and a contract account has an address of the same form.
Every Solana account has an address of 32 bytes, either an Ed25519 public key or one derived from a program, and it is written as a base58 string.
A TRON address is 21 bytes that begin with the byte 0x41, and wallets and explorers show it in Base58Check as 34 characters starting with T.
basis.source: TRON Developer Hub: Accounts and keys

findings.message: Payment P-017 pays in DAI, which is not in the list of tokens the batch may pay in (USDC and USDT; --tokens sets another). This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Pay in a token of the list, or give the tokens your team pays in with --tokens.
findings.own: a list of tokens a batch may pay in is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the default list is the tool's own and --tokens sets yours

findings.message: The batch holds the key "seedPhrase", which names a seed, a mnemonic or a private key. The tool never reads one, and the value is not shown.
findings.fix: Remove the value from the file and from wherever the file was copied, treat it as exposed and move the funds it controls. A payout batch names wallets by their public address only.

findings.message: The rail of payment P-021 is "wire"; it must be bank or stablecoin.
findings.fix: Write the value as docs/inputs.md shows: text for names, codes, accounts and addresses, decimal numbers for amounts and rates.

findings.message: Payment P-022 is a bank payment with no currency.
findings.fix: Add the field named; docs/inputs.md lists what each payment needs.

findings.message: The iban of payment P-004 is an account in BE, but the beneficiaryCountry is AT. Either can be right, as a beneficiary may bank abroad, but a wrong country is also how a payment reaches the wrong account. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Check the beneficiary country and the IBAN with the beneficiary; when the account is abroad on purpose, keep the warning and say so in the review.

basis.text: Some prefixes of the registry stand for other territories as well: Aland banks under FI, the Isle of Man, Jersey and Guernsey under GB, and the French overseas departments and territories under FR.

findings.own: comparing the country of the IBAN with the beneficiary country is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a beneficiary may hold an account abroad, and the registry only says which territories a prefix covers

findings.message: The bic of payment P-006, EXMPDEFF, is of a bank in DE, but the beneficiaryCountry is CH and the iban is in CH. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Check the BIC with the beneficiary; when the bank is abroad on purpose, keep the warning and say so in the review.

basis.text: ISO 9362 defines the BIC as eight characters, four letters or digits for the party, two letters for a country code of ISO 3166-1 and two letters or digits after them, with a branch code of three more characters that may be added.

findings.own: comparing the country of the BIC with the beneficiary country is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the BIC page gives the place of the country code, not a rule that the bank and the beneficiary share a country

findings.message: Payment P-012 pays 1500 EUR to the same account as payment P-001 at line 19, for the same amount. It may be one payment written twice. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Check that the two payments are meant; remove one when the same payment was written twice.
findings.own: looking for two payments of one amount to one account is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; two such payments can be right, such as two invoices of the same amount

findings.message: The beneficiaryName of payment P-014 is "Q", with fewer than 3 letters, too short to screen against sanctions lists or to match to the account holder. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Write the full name of the beneficiary, not initials or a placeholder.
findings.own: the least length of a name is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; three letters is the tool's own floor, and a real name can be that short

findings.message: Payment P-015 is paid in USD from EUR, the debitCurrency of the batch, and gives no fxRate, so the amount debited is not known until the bank converts it. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Give the rate the batch was priced at in fxRate, so that the amount debited is known before the batch is sent.
findings.own: asking for the rate of a converted payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a bank can convert at its own rate, and the batch then debits an amount no one checked

findings.message: Payment P-018 pays in USDT on Base, a pair the tool's table does not list, so the token may be a bridged copy or not exist on the network. Check the token contract of the issuer by hand. This is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites.
findings.fix: Check by hand that the issuer of the token lists a contract on the network, and how a wallet address on it is written.
